packageRules.description: Never digest-pin the self-referential reusable workflow in renovate-changeset.yml. It is invoked `@main` on purpose: the reusable job's OIDC `job_workflow_ref` claim must equal the AWS minter role's StringEquals-pinned `…@refs/heads/main` (docs/cicd/renovate-integration.md §7). `helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests` would rewrite it to a commit SHA, breaking `sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` so minting fails on every Renovate PR (this happened in #152). This is an in-repo self-reference on a protected branch, so SHA immutability buys nothing here.

Auto-merge non-major updates once all required checks pass (CI build/lint/test, merge-checks, the Socket supply-chain scanner, changeset-present). Majors are deliberately absent from `matchUpdateTypes`, so they never auto-merge and always get a human. The build-scripts rule below overrides this back to manual; patched-deps inherit it (they self-gate — a broken patch fails CI). Security updates auto-merge regardless via `vulnerabilityAlerts`.

Packages with install/build scripts (pnpm `allowBuilds` in pnpm-workspace.yaml) run arbitrary code on install. Pull each out of the `group:allNonMajor` batch into its own PR with a distinct title/label, and never auto-merge — so the script-running bump is reviewed in isolation. Keep this list in sync with `allowBuilds`.

Packages with a pnpm patch (`patchedDependencies` in pnpm-workspace.yaml) carry a version-pinned patch; a bump usually leaves the patch unapplied and breaks the lockfile relock (`pnpm install` fails). Pull each out of the `group:allNonMajor` batch into its own PR with a distinct title/label so a broken patch doesn't sink the batch — but don't force manual merge: a broken patch fails CI and waits for a human to re-roll or drop it, while a bump that still applies cleanly (e.g. an unversioned patch) rides the non-major auto-merge rule above. `matchPackageNames` is kept in sync with `patchedDependencies` by repo-kit; do not edit it by hand.

`minecraft-test-lib` derives its whole shipped surface from these two at build time — the fake classes and manifests from `@minecraft/server`, the vanilla id lists a preset registers from `@minecraft/vanilla-data` — and states the versions it answers for. A bump changes what the package claims, so it never auto-merges: a human reads the regenerated diff and moves the counts the tests write out. Renovate installs with `--ignore-scripts` and commits only its changeset, so the generated files in its PR are stale by construction; regenerate locally before reviewing.

MobX and its React bindings peer-pin each other and are released in lockstep: `mobx-react-lite@4` requires `mobx ^6.9.0`, `mobx-react-lite@5` requires `mobx ^7.0.0` (same for `mobx-react` 9/10). Split across separate PRs, whichever lands first leaves the pair mismatched — and CI does not catch it, because `mobx-react-lite` is imported only by refbash's `observer` components while its suite covers hooks alone: `mobx-react-lite@5` on `mobx@6` throws `mobx-react-lite requires mobx at least version 7` at module load, yet build, typecheck, and every test still pass on a TUI that cannot start (#381/#382). Grouping keeps the peer-locked bump in one reviewable PR. `separateMajorMinor: false` holds them together when only one side has a major, which is the case that split them; the group also pulls their non-majors out of the `group:allNonMajor` batch, where they still ride the auto-merge rule above.
repo-kit templates all .nvmrc files; a Renovate bump is reverted by `pnpm sync` and fails the merge-checks gate
engines.node / engines.pnpm are written by repo-kit (.repo-kit.yml); updating them fails the sync gate
tsdown's version is owned by repo-kit (.repo-kit.yml), not Renovate

TypeScript is held at v6 because typescript-eslint cannot run against v7. TS 7 is the native port: the `typescript` package's main entry exports only `version` and `versionMajorMinor`, and the classic compiler API moved to `typescript/unstable/*`. `@typescript-eslint/typescript-estree` reads `ts.ModuleKind.Cjs` at module load, so ESLint dies with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'Cjs')` before linting a file — that is every package's `lint` task and every lint-staged hook. The peer range is `>=4.8.4 <6.1.0` on every published version including canary (checked at 8.66.x, 2026-08-09), so there is no version to move to yet. Raise the ceiling once typescript-eslint supports v7; `nodejs/minecraft/test-lib/tools/generate.ts` must be ported off the classic compiler API in the same change.
